profile.campus: Ashburn, VA Data Center Alley (Guilford Drive cluster)
profile.reading:
This facility is mapped as Level 3 Ashburn, retaining the pre-Lumen brand name, at 44633 Guilford Drive, Ashburn, VA 20147, sitting directly amid the Guilford Drive cluster where NTT's VA1 (44664) and VA2 (44610) buildings, tracked elsewhere in this registry, are also located; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Level 3 Communications was acquired by CenturyLink on November 1, 2017 and the combined company was renamed Lumen Technologies on September 14, 2020; some legacy facility signage and mapping records, including this one, still carry the pre-merger Level 3 name. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility, including network-edge buildings like this one alongside the wholesale campuses nearby. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027; regulators approved $775.6 million of the roughly $1.2 billion Dominion sought, cutting about $350 million tied to speculative data center projects, according to Inside Climate News.

This Guilford Drive building sits directly inside the same Ashburn block as several NTT buildings tracked elsewhere in this registry, illustrating how Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley" packs network-edge colocation providers like Lumen alongside multi-hundred-megawatt wholesale campuses within the same few blocks.

reading.body:
Level 3 Ashburn is a carrier-neutral colocation site operated by Lumen Technologies on Guilford Drive in Ashburn, Virginia, where it sits directly alongside NTT's VA1 and VA2 wholesale data center campuses. Lumen does not publish IT capacity, square footage, or power draw for this facility or any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites, disclosing only a general cabinet power range of 3 to 15 kilowatts per unit that varies by location. Without published specifications, this facility cannot be ranked or sized relative to Virginia's wholesale AI infrastructure.

Ashburn's role in AI scaling depends on electricity rates set by regulators who now shape the economics of every building in the market. In November 2026, Virginia regulators approved new Dominion Energy rates that carved out a dedicated GS-5 rate class for data centers effective January 2027, while cutting roughly $350 million in cost recovery tied to speculative projects, according to Inside Climate News. These rate changes apply to network-edge colocation providers like this one as directly as to wholesale campuses, reshaping the financial viability of any tenant seeking power density in this cluster.

This facility's strategic value lies in network adjacency rather than published scale. Its location in the same Guilford Drive block as multiple hundred-megawatt wholesale campuses positions it to serve as edge colocation for AI workloads that require proximity to wholesale infrastructure, though Lumen's non-disclosure of per-building capacity leaves its role in Virginia's 1,375 MW of published data center power opaque. Of Virginia's 330 mapped facilities, only 23 publish megawatt figures; this site contributes no public data to that count.
